name: What is the difference between a Jacuzzi, hot tub, and built-in spa?

mainEntity.name: What is the real difference between a Jacuzzi, a hot tub, and a built-in spa when planning construction?
mainEntity.text: What is the real difference between a Jacuzzi, a hot tub, and a built-in spa when planning construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: In construction conversations, people often say Jacuzzi when they mean any jetted spa. Technically, Jacuzzi is a brand name, while hot tub usually refers to a portable, self-contained unit. A built-in spa is different because it becomes part of the property’s hardscape or pool design and requires excavation, plumbing, electrical work, waterproofing, and finishing. That difference matters because costs, permits, maintenance, and design flexibility are not the same. A portable hot tub is faster to install and easier to replace, but it offers less customization. A built-in spa can be matched to the architecture of a Los Angeles home and finished in stone, plaster, or tile, but it needs more planning and a larger budget. Homeowners should decide whether the goal is portability, aesthetics, therapy features, or long-term resale value. Contractors should clarify this early because the scope changes completely depending on whether the project is a product install or a custom construction build.
acceptedAnswer.description: A Jacuzzi is often used generically to describe a jetted spa, but technically it is a brand name. A hot tub is usually a freestanding, portable unit, while a built-in spa is constructed into the ground, decking, or pool design and requires more site work.
